about: Château Meyney sits on a gentle rise above the Gironde estuary in Saint-Estèphe, its 51 hectares of vines in a single block between Montrose and Calon-Ségur. Monks were tending vines here in the Middle Ages, and in the 17th century the Feuillant order made it a model estate, finishing the “maison du Meyney” in 1662. The négociant Désiré Cordier bought it in 1919 and planted the Petit Verdot that still marks its wines. Since 2004 it has belonged to the Crédit Agricole group, with Anne Le Naour leading the estate.

The vines grow on Garonne gravel over clay and limestone, crossed by a rare vein of blue clay about three metres deep, the same subsoil found at Pétrus, which feeds the vines water through dry spells. For 2018, a warm, sunny year, the grapes were picked by hand between late September and mid-October, sorted closely and fermented plot by plot after a few days of cold soaking. Part of the wine finished its malolactic fermentation in new barrels, and the whole grand vin was aged in French oak, 35% of it new.

The 2018 leans more than usual on Petit Verdot, at 18% of the blend, alongside Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. That gives the wine its depth of colour, its spice and its firm frame. Critics singled it out in this celebrated vintage: Decanter and Wine Enthusiast each gave it 94 points, and James Suckling 95, describing a structured, long-lived Saint-Estèphe with dark fruit and real grip.
facts: 51 ha in one block on gravel over blue clay
HVE level 3 and ISO 14001; organic conversion begun 2021
